HRA Analysis: BEYOND DOUBT (7) was a very impressive winner last time out sitting without cover and just proving too good at this track and trip. HES ALL TORQUE (6) has been excellent in recent outings. He was able to overcome a 40 metre handicap last time out in the Showcase series and broke the track record winning well. He draws well and is likely to press forward and look to race in a prominent position. BUDDY PERFECT (5) was able to lead and win three starts ago at Redcliffe rating reasonable time. He may be able to press forward and find the lead again before having options from there. MAJOR CRUNCH (2) has excellent gate speed and may be able to zip across before taking a sit on one of the better chances. He was running on well last start after putting in a poor run his start prior sitting leaders back and fading out of it late. SELECTIONS: BEYOND DOUBT (7), HES ALL TORQUE (6), BUDDY PERFECT (5), MAJOR CRUNCH (2) SUGGESTED BET: BUDDY PERFECT (5) each way.

CATSEYE BEACH (1) burned very hard to lead two starts ago and was beaten just 5.2 metres by the in-form Attachment who is set to go around a short-priced favourite in the open class pace later in the card. He and was just run down by Double Lou in late June. He should lead and take all kinds of running down in this race. AIR EXPRESS (8) should get a good run through behind the likely leader in the race. He followed through nicely two starts ago and was able to run fourth behind Rakasandy not beaten too far. He should get the right run and can be running on late. SMARTER THAN YOU (9) was left without cover and wasn’t beaten too far by Fate Awaits in a race which didn’t suit runners off the pegs. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late. EXCLUSIVE HUSTLER (3) couldn’t quite show enough gate speed last time out to hold out Rakasandy who was able to lead all the way. He draws less favourably this time and is set for what looks to be quite a tough run on paper. SELECTIONS: CATSEYE BEACH (1), AIR EXPRESS (8), SMARTER THAN YOU (9), EXCLUSIVE HUSTLER (3) SUGGESTED BET: CATSEYE BEACH (1) to win.

BETTERTHANFEDERER (3) is a capable sit sprinter that appears quite well suited in this race from a low front row draw. He won his first two for Tom Callaghan before doing things wrong last time out after working hard. STARZZZDESTINY (10) found the top recently at this track and trip and was run down in good time by Mister Manager. He gets less favours from a back row draw this time but should still be thereabouts. SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (1) impressed in NSW three starts ago when sitting without cover and proving too good. He was just fair when having his first QLD start last time out but does draw to get plenty of favours this time. FOXFIRE EASTON (5) started off a 30 metre handicap two starts ago and was too good there. He may be shuffled back again in this race and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: BETTERTHANFEDERER (3), STARZZZDESTINY (10), SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (1), FOXFIRE EASTON (5) SUGGESTED BET: BETTERTHANFEDERER (3) to win.

MAGNETIC STORM (2) wasn’t asked to do much in a recent trial when following them around before pulling out late and running through the line well. He has had two weeks since that trial and should be fitter. His best form would see him hard to beat in a race of this nature. DUAL CAM (1) has gate speed which should give him options in this race. He attempted to cross last time out but wasn’t able to get over and was left off the pegs in a race dominated by runners up on speed. STUDLEIGH MARK (8) secured a good run last time out and was able to run over the top late to beat Sweet Rocky over the 1660. He should be suited by the inside back row draw and can be running on late in this race. GREAT ACHIEVER (9) finished the race off fairly last time out after sitting on the leaders back last time out at this track. He should find this race a bit easier and draws to do no work early. SELECTIONS: MAGNETIC STORM (2), DUAL CAM (1), STUDLEIGH MARK (8), GREAT ACHIEVER (9) SUGGESTED BET: MAGNETIC STORM (2) to win.

GOLDEN SHOOZ (7) bounced back to form last time out when leading and winning by a huge margin there. Given that race was the second division of the Qualifying race she gets into the same race again this week against the mares this time and looks hard to beat again. ALWAYS ADORNED (2) has gate speed and may look to press forward early before having options from there. She was running on well into third last time out at Redcliffe in a race taken out by Nitrator who ran a very slick last half. She should be thereabouts. HARPERVILLE (3) was having her first run since late July last time out when running on fairly late into fifth. She draws more favourably this time and is seemingly a horse which likes to race up on speed. THE LADY DIOR (5) finished third behind Miss Bay King Cole last time out after being forced to do the work outside the leader which isn’t a position she is usually suited to in races. She may be left to do some work again but should run well. SELECTIONS: GOLDEN SHOOZ (7), ALWAYS ADORNED (2), HARPERVILLE (3), THE LADY DIOR (5) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDEN SHOOZ (7) to win.

DOVE LAKE (1) got back in the run last time out in a stronger race and was running through the line nicely late into sixth. She comes into this race third up from a spell and should be nearing peak fitness. PRINCESS ARNA (8) should get a good run through in this race behind a horse which is likely to be keen to hold a forward position. She was a winner three starts ago leading all the way and rating good time. OUR ULTIMATE MILLY (5) handed over to Sheer Vitality last time out and was able to run second to that horse at Redcliffe. She draws awkwardly in this race and will need a few things to go her way in the run. MOVE HEAVENNEARTH (9) secured a good run leaders back last time out and was running on well into third behind Sporty Zara. She is likely to get a good run off the speed and can be running on late again. SELECTIONS: DOVE LAKE (1), PRINCESS ARNA (8), OUR ULTIMATE MILLY (5), MOVE HEAVENNEARTH (9) SUGGESTED BET: DOVE LAKE (1) to win.

ATTACHMENT (5) has won four in a row and looks set to be very hard to beat in another suitable race. He has great gate speed and can look to fly across early and take it up which should see him hard to run down in this race. TIMS A TROOPER (1) may be suited by the step back up to 2138 in this race after closing strongly late last time out to just miss second in a similar field. He may be shuffled back early and should be running on strongly late. WISPER A SECRET (3) has brilliant gate speed and should be able to zip across before sitting on his stablemate ATTACHMENT (5) again. He was good enough to hang on for second last time out and will be looking to do the same again. DASHING (6) was excellent in a recent trial when not beaten far by Captain Shuffles in fast time. He draws poorly in this race and will need the race run to suit to be figuring in the finish. SELECTIONS: ATTACHMENT (5), TIMS A TROOPER (1), WISPER A SECRET (3), DASHING (6) SUGGESTED BET: TIMS A TROOPER (1) to place.

GOLDEN FIRE (3) has brilliant gate speed and is likely to attempt to zip across early before having options from there. She was able to burn across last time out over the 2138 before taking a sit on Sally Bigtime and running second. She is likely to be suited back to 1660 and should be hard to beat. SALLY BIGTIME (6) was able to work to the lead last time out over the 2138 taking them all the way holding off the late challenge of GOLDEN FIRE (3). This race appears likely to pan out similar on paper and she should run well again. TREMENDOUS SENSATION (1) didn’t have much luck last time out when crossed early before being checked when that horse galloped. She has the same draw again in this race which could see her crossed and shuffled back needing a few things to go her way in the run. LUVARECHS (2) was forced to race without cover last time out against similar company and battled on well there for sixth. She appears likely to be suited by the step back in distance and draws well in this race. SELECTIONS: GOLDEN FIRE (3), SALLY BIGTIME (6), TREMENDOUS SENSATION (1), LUVARECHS (2) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDEN FIRE (3) to win. OVERVIEW:BOSS MAJOR (1) hasn’t been at his best form for some time but he is perfectly drawn in a suitable race and has the services of leading reinsman James Herbertson so he gets his chance to improve. JOEYS HANGOVER (6) is resuming since a third at Shepparton in June. He is a fast beginner and he is usually competitive against this class so he is worth an investment. ALLTHEWAYTOROYALTY (4) was runner up at Ballarat on August 05 and has joined local trainer Michael Gadsden since his latest unplaced performance. He is worth thought under these conditions. MY LUCKY ROCK (2) is resuming since a fifth at Melton in July 2025. She lacks recent racing but she was racing in reasonable form at the end of her last preparation so she has claims if she is somewhere near her peak. She raced without cover when a reasonable fourth at a Maryborough trial effort last week. SELECTIONS: BOSS MAJOR (1), JOEYS HANGOVER (6), ALLTHEWAYROYALTY (4), MY LUCKY ROCK (2)

OVERVIEW:OVER THE LINE (6) led out then took cover and was held up for momentum on the home turn before using the sprint lane when she finished second behind Chainsmoke at Swan Hill last week. She should be getting close to her peak form after having two starts back from a break and is worth following. FLEUR BELLA (1) has performed nicely in three starts since coming from New South Wales and was able to lead throughout at Mildura last outing. She is drawn to lead again and should take catching. TORQUE INTHEUSA (7) has had a few chances since returning from South Australia but he is dropping back into a more suitable class now and he met a smart one in Farroh Joe at Stawell last outing so he warrants consideration. SKIPPYS DELIGHT (5) was runner up in a slick mile of 1.54.8 at Geelong two starts ago and is not without a chance under these conditions. SELECTIONS: OVER THE LINE (6), FLEUR BELLA (1), TORQUE INTHEUSA (7), SKIPPYS DELIGHT (5)

OVERVIEW: ELLI JOH (8) recorded a personal best mile rate of 1.57.3 when she scored at Hamilton then followed with a handy second behind Justlikedave in fast time at Cranbourne. She is awkwardly drawn but will find this race to be no harder. ESPERANZA (7) led out then took cover and used the sprint lane when a close second behind Major Lincoln at Stawell last outing. She scored at Kilmore three starts ago and she should give another bold showing under these conditions. THE LADYBIRD (4) finished off well for third at Wagga two starts ago then missed out at Kilmore last outing. She can sprint to the line quickly with the right trail forward and is worth thought. TASTE IT (5) and SKADI (6) have both won against similar grade recently and are not without a chance. SELECTIONS: ELLI JOH (8), ESPERANZA (7), THE LADYBIRD (4), SKADI (6)

OVERVIEW: ARZALI ROCKSTAR (6) will appreciate a massive drop back in class on her past three performances during the Super Series. She made it through to the Group 1 Final and she defeated a reasonable field at a Ballarat victory in July so she should prove hard to beat against this line up. JUST LIKE NUGGET (5) continues to race consistently and was held up for a run at a vital stage when he finished off well for third behind Farroh Joe at Stawell last week. He should run his usual honest race. OPERTSER (1) continues to improve with the benefit of racing and went to the line jogging with no clear run when an unlucky fourth at Cranbourne last week. He is drawn to trail the likely leader SMOKING SHANNON (2) and should be finishing fast along the passing lane. SMOKING SHANNON (2) is a fast beginner and performs best when she is able to lead. She does prefer competing over the sprint distance but she is worth thought from her good draw. BACK: ARZALI ROCKSTAR (6) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: ARZALI ROCKSTAR (6), JUST LIKE NUGGET (5), OPERTSER (1), SMOKING SHANNON (2)

OVERVIEW:AMADA VILLMA (2) is a fast beginner and is a good chance of attempting an all of the way victory from her good draw over the sprint distance. She was shuffled to three back on the markers mid-race and moved up without cover at the 900m mark when a creditable third at Swan Hill last outing. MISS ADELIA (1) raced without cover throughout and did well for second behind Queens Boulevard at Stawell on debut. She should have improved by the experience and she is ideally drawn so she is capable of going one better. EVIE KATE (4) finished off nicely in a last quarter of 28.1 seconds when a close second at a Maryborough trial effort last week and appears to have a promising future. CAPTAIN MILO (7) trailed the leader and was held up badly for a run when an unlucky fifth behind Piastri at Shepparton last week. He missed out narrowly at Kilmore prior and he has claims despite being drawn on the outside of the front line. ARZALI SHACARRI (8) was beaten by a long way on debut but the time was fast and this race appears to be a little easier. The first starter PHILS BOY (3) has shown ability in several trial efforts andmust be kept safe. SELECTIONS: AMADA VILLMA (2), MISS ADELIA (1), EVIE KATE (4), CAPTAIN MILO (7)

OVERVIEW:RAPTA (6) finished fifth in a heat of the Super Series then followed with a fifth in the Final (Group 1) so he will appreciate a massive drop back in class for this assignment. He wasn’t beaten by far behind Howdy Mate in the Super Series Final so he was far from disgraced and should make his presence felt here. EL UNO (2) is resuming since July but he recorded handy time at an easy trial victory at Maryborough last week and is drawn to go well. ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8) settled three back on the markers, moved up without cover at the 800m and hit the front approaching the home turn before being run down late when second behind Alectrona at Cranbourne last outing. He is awkwardly drawn but should be working home well. FRANKS ALOT (5) finished off nicely for fourth behind the smart mare Little Miss Morgan at a Shepparton trial performance and is not to be underestimated. SKYE DIVA (4) has performed fairly well at the trials and must be kept safe. BACK: RAPTA (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RAPTA (6), EL UNO (2), ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8), FRANKS ALOT (5)

OVERVIEW: CHAMPAGNE CHARLEY (10) was resuming since February when he finished off solidly for a close second at Kilmore. He faces a big handicap but he should be fitter and he is a proven winner from the standing start so he warrants respect. KAMARAN (9) can make mistakes occasionally but he is a smart horse when he can put it altogether. He pushed around the field mid-race to park without cover from the 900m when a game second behind Majestic Tooth in a mile rate of 1.57.7 at his latest appearance. BOUTIKA (7) is stepping up in class but is racing in career best form and broke the track record when she won at Ararat two starts ago so she cannot be underestimated. WATCH AND ACT (8) is a quick beginner and boasts a handy standing start record so he rates as a value hope. CONNIES PRESIDENT (5) and POPPY POPSTAR (6) are both capable of showing up without surprising. SELECTIONS: CHAMPAGNE CHARLEY (10), KAMARAN (9), BOUTIKA (7), WATCH AND ACT (8)

OVERVIEW: TOPSIE BEWARE (4) won convincingly at Ararat when on debut back in March then was spelled. She has had numerous trials leading up to her second attempt and she scored at the Bacchus Marsh trials last week so she must be respected. OWEN THE SAINTS (9) recorded a handy mile rate of 1.56.7 when he scored at Kilmore on September 03 and was held up for a run at a vital stage at his latest unlucky third. He follows out behind a reasonable beginner and will be hard to hold out in the run to the finish. SPORTING RAGE (8) is likely to be shuffled back on the markers from the inside of the second line but he is racing well enough to figure in the finish. He won from behind the leader at Charlton two starts ago and should be finding the line strongly again. FIVE CENT (2) is a grinding type that performs best when he is close to the pace. He will prove hard to beat if he can work forward to find the lead shortly after the start. BACK: TOPSIE BEWARE (4) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: TOPSIE BEWARE (4), OWEN THE SAINTS (9), SPORTING RAGE (8), FIVE CENT (2)

OVERVIEW: OUR SWEET JEANNIE (3) is a smart filly, which has been racing in the Super Series with her latest performance being a sixth behind Bettor Beach in the Final. She is versatile and should make her presence felt from the good draw. LEONARD (1) led throughout in a handy mile rate of 1.55.1 at Swan Hill last week and is perfectly drawn again. This is a field of more depth but he should be competitive again. TELEMACHUS (11) is poorly drawn but he appears to be very well graded in this event. He progressed forward to find the lead when a close up fourth behind Blake Bolac at Metropolitan level last outing. KATUNGA EXPRESS (8) has the perfect trailing draw behind LEONARD (1) and possesses a handy finishing burst so he rates as a value hope. TOPSIES BLING (9) sprinted sharply to win in slick time at Ballarat last outing and has won a trial since. She is a speedy mare and is not without a chance. BACK: OUR SWEET JEANNIE (3) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: OUR SWEET JEANNIE (3), LEONARD (1), TELEMACHUS (11), KATUNGA EXPRESS (8)

OVERVIEW:CHINSKI (4) is having his first start at Echuca but based on his racing pattern, should love the circuit. He finds a draw to use his gate speed and find the top over the short distance, which is a huge advantage on the tighter track with the shorter straight. He was a winner two starts back, where he unsuccessfully challenged for the lead before coming again to win. His mobile record is strong and, if the map works out, he’ll take some catching. JILLIBY TOPGUN (9) has plenty of upside based on what he’s been able to produce this season, winning five from 16, and the concession claim of Tasmyn Potter brings him well in on the ratings scale. His last performance at this track saw him do work and be beaten a distance, so whilst he’s better suited on the bigger tracks, he’s in the mix. MAJESTIC MONARCH (10) is also well graded with the claim, but he is coming off a very disappointing run at Shepparton last week, where he was well supported, led and dropped out. His form prior was good, so if you can overlook last time, he’s a genuine chance. WHATS THE TEA (3) is having his first try here and gets the services of ace reinsman James Herbertson. He needs to be better than last start, but this is easier. KALARNEY PRINCE (2) also has minor claims, as his tactical speed should see him map in a favourable position. BACK: CHINSKI (4) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:CHINSKI (4), JILLIBY TOPGUN (9), MAJESTIC MONARCH (10), WHATS THE TEA (3)

OVERVIEW:ARRAPS (5) is a speedy beginner and looks well served from the draw to press forward aggressively and look for the top end against this opposition. His track and distance profile is also strong for a race of this calibre, and his past two runs leading into this have been very good. The work he had to do last time and the sectionals he was able to produce suggest he can be too strong for these. WHERES WOOD WOOD (11) caught many by surprise last week when he was able to lead and dash away, running good time at Shepparton. In fairness, he has been consistent overall this season, and although his set-up is completely different this time, his record at this track commands respect. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6) can be a little hard to catch, but his performance three starts back to win at Shepparton was good enough to be competitive here. It’s hard to know how he maps and his last two runs have been poor, but he’s worth keeping safe. STELLAR QUEEN (1) and FOUR STARZZZ RUBY (3) are the other speed influences off the front row, and the right map gives them claims, particularly at the minor end. SELECTIONS:ARRAPS (5), WHERES WOOD WOOD (11), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6), STELLAR QUEEN (1)

OVERVIEW:SOHO PLAYGIRL (4) was terrific last week in winning at her first run for the new stable, where she let down with a powerful finishing burst. Her career profile suggests her best performances come when she can draw to race handy, and the map may be in her favour here. She has a good strike rate at the track and, if she can back up what she did last week, will be hard to hold out. STARZINHEREYES (3) is a quick beginner suited to this track and distance. Her past two runs back in more suitable grade have been very good, and those efforts have come with Luke Dunne in the sulky, who sticks with her here. ELIZAJANE (6) is flying, winning her past couple when able to lead and running good time in both. BULLETPROOF KID (5) has been a model of consistency this campaign and got a deserved win when able to lead at Cranbourne two starts back. This map is a little sticky, but he’s certainly in the mix. SELECTIONS:SOHO PLAYGIRL (4), STARZINHEREYES (3), ELIZAJANE (6), BULLETPROOF KID (5)

OVERVIEW: ALTO CORRAGIO (3) has been runner-up in both career starts, both over 2190m at Shepparton. On debut he showed gate speed, led and was beaten only a half-head. Last week he came from the second row and was narrowly beaten again. He has a strong trainer/driver combination and, with a positive map over a similar middle distance against an easier field, it heavily favours him breaking through. MAJOR FRIEND (1) is the obvious danger and gets the map advantage. She’s placed six times from nine starts, including four of her past five, and has already shown the ability to trail the top pick and get her chance. She came through the same race last week but didn’t have much luck. Those two clearly stand out. SLOWBURN (7) is a 2yo from the Riverina whose two performances to date boast a solid SP profile, and those runs have been okay. Likely to be three pegs means minor consideration is more realistic. JUST MY LUCK (4) needs to lift on what he’s displayed, but there have been glimpses of ability to suggest he can improve against a moderate line-up. BACK: ALTO CORRAGIO (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:ALTO CORRAGIO (3), MAJOR FRIEND (1), SLOWBURN (7), JUST MY LUCK (4)

OVERVIEW:FERRIGNO (2) hasn’t won since October last year, but there’s a strong case to be made for him breaking that run of outs. He’s been racing up in grade for quite a while and, furthermore, hasn’t had the best set-up to put his best foot forward, which is when he’s able to lead. He’s having his first look at Echuca, but his tactical speed can see him get back to his best. TARA VICTORY (8) has been performing well for her in-form stable, and when she found a suitable grade two starts back, she won easily. She should map quite well trailing out the top pick, so although she’s going to have to earn it from off the speed, she’s a strong chance. HELLOVATIME (6) is another in great form and nearly went all the way last week. His record this campaign is excellent, and he has gone close in two tries at this track; he will just need luck from the draw. DRESSED IN GOLD (4) is yet to win this preparation but is showing signs that a win isn’t far away. This is quality opposition, though, while MICHEN ROY (5) had to work hard last week and dropped out, but he’s honest and won’t be far away. BACK: FERRIGNO (2) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: FERRIGNO (2), TARA VICTORY (8), HELLOVATIME (6), DRESSED IN GOLD (4)

OVERVIEW: A tricky map to work out here, but if REGAL ROCK (5) can get across, he will be hard to run down. His two runs this campaign have been solid in harder company, where he found the top and battled on well. This is significantly easier and, if he gets to the peg line, he’s capable of running faster times than the opposition. DOT BALL (7) has the challenge of overcoming the back row, but if there’s a strong battle for the lead, he will be the beneficiary. He’s won two of his past four, drops in grade and is a winner at this track. ALPHA CRUCIS (3) could be the one open to sharp improvement on his numerical form, finding a suitable draw and set-up. He’s a winner at this track and, with the right map, he’ll be in the finish. Then at the minor end, SWISS LIGHTNING (1) can map softly, while KRAKEY (4) goes okay at this level but is fresh-up here and the map is sticky. SELECTIONS: REGAL ROCK (5), DOT BALL (7), ALPHA CRUCIS (3), KRAKEY (4)

OVERVIEW:BIG RAIN (1) is a 14-start maiden, but she has placed eight times and this, by far, looks to be her most suitable assignment. She has natural gate speed, which has seen her lead at her past three starts, and here at Echuca she looks well suited with the shorter straight to cling on. She won’t strike a more winnable race. MI BOW (3) is a 35-start maiden and has placed 17 times. She’s getting closer and has a strong SP profile for a race of this calibre, while the Herbertson factor is a plus. SPESHAL (7) is also racing well without winning, and her failures at her past two have been a result of galloping out. If she can get away and map behind the leader, she’s a chance. GREAT HORIZON (2) doesn’t threaten to win, but she is reliable in her gait, so if others get it wrong, she can be the last one standing. BACK: BIG RAIN (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BIG RAIN (1), MI BOW (3), SPESHAL (7), GREAT HORIZON (2)

OVERVIEW:FINAL BOW (3) has 36 career wins and, crucially, an exceptional Echuca record of 14 starts for five wins. She won consecutive races at Shepparton before the Maryborough failure and bounced back with a second last week, where the leader was off and gone by the time she made her run. She can map more positively from this draw and, if she finds the top, will be hard to run down. MAMMALS REASON (5) is a model of consistency with two wins and three placings from her past five. The concern is how she maps from the draw, but her form is good enough to be a winning hope. HIGHVIEW HAMMER (1) is a quick beginner and normally likes to take cover, so gets the ideal map from barrier 1. His last win in June came when he was able to sit leader’s back. SPORTS WRACK (6) keeps threatening to bounce back to form as he continues to drop in grade. The draw here hurts, but he’s one who is ready to win in this grade when things work out. BACK: FINAL BOW (3)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:FINAL BOW (3), MAMMALS REASON (5), HIGHVIEW HAMMER (1), SPORTS WRACK (6)

STOLEN ONE (1) gets the advantage from the pole draw after two super-impressive victories in handy time throughout the Sweepstakes series. She takes on the boys here, but with the draw advantage she looks the horse to beat. HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (3) was good first up from a break after doing some work early and still running a slick last half before being run down late by a handy one. Tactics will be interesting here, but his class should take him a long way and give the expected favourite a run for her money. OUR ROB ROY (2) has also shown good ability thus far in his career and should be suited settling closer along the pegs. He showed a brilliant turn of foot two starts back, producing a very fast quarter to nearly win, and will be looking to do something similar here. SOLO STITCH (4) is the most experienced runner in the field and continues to produce competitive performances, but may lack the class of some of his rivals here, especially from the widest draw where he is likely to settle last. Selections:STOLEN ONE (1), HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (3), OUR ROB ROY (2), SOLO STITCH (4)

The standing-start event sees brilliant beginner ALBERIO (2) likely to ping away and be first to the pegs, where he will have options from there. He looks to get his chance to finish on the podium after racing somewhat below his best over the past few months. SPORTZSILK (1) attempts the stand for the first time, and his first-up run for the new stable last week was good enough to see him in the finish here if he steps cleanly. REPETITIVE (4) is normally a good beginner and went close to winning last start when second against a similar field, so should be thereabouts again. SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6) returned to the winner's circle last week when making a mid-race move and proving far too strong. Similar tactics may be adopted again here, which would make him one of the hardest to beat. The 20-metre runners WE SALUTE YOU (7) and JOHN VINCENT (8) are clearly the class horses of the field and have been racing competitively in stronger company than they meet here. It's always difficult to make up ground over the middle-distance standing start, but their class should take them a long way. Selections:SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6), WE SALUTE YOU (7), JOHN VINCENT (8), SPORTZSILK (1)

RESURGENT WARRIOR (2) should be able to cross to the pegs and lead over the short distance, which should give him his best chance of winning. SHADES OF SILK (3) looks likely to again have to do the hard yards outside the leader, but has battled on gamely in good time at his past few starts and should do the same again here. JET TO HEAVEN (1) again draws the pole and should get every chance along the pegs late. JUST LIKA DREAM (4) and LADY IN LINE (5) may have to be driven with a sit and will be relying on genuine tempo and a nice run into the race to be finishing home strongly, as will GOBSMACKED (7), who draws the outside gate but rattled home to win last start. KENYA (8) draws his worst possible gate, with his best racing normally coming when driven hard on speed. He may be forced to stay three pegs here and hope for an even tempo, but if the gaps appear late, he will be right in the finish. Selections:RESURGENT WARRIOR (2), SHADES OF SILK (3), KENYA (8), JET TO HEAVEN (1)

TALK IS CHEAP (7) was a tough winner last start after copping pressure early when leading and still proving too strong by over nine metres late. She draws a wide gate here and rises slightly in class, but would only need to reproduce that effort to be right in the finish again. REALLY SMARTIE (5) is an eight-year-old gelding making his first start for Team McKenzie after arriving from Victoria. He has mixed his form over time but clearly possesses the ability to be in the finish if he can produce something near his best. Another runner making their state debut is OUR DANCE MONKEY (1), who competed in strong races as a younger horse and has been competitive against better classed horses than she meets here. She is aided by the pole draw and looks a good chance to break through for the new stable off her latest trial effort. DENVER MAN (9) returns to the state, where his most recent victory came last October. He has been misbehaving of late, but if he brings his best manners, he should be running home strongly from the nice trailing draw. DOLCE DRAMA (4) was well backed when second last start and, with another nice run in transit, should be finishing home strongly again. BUSLOAD OF FAITH (6) produced an improved effort last start when sitting outside the leader over the short distance and will no doubt again look to roll forward from his draw, although he does have a tendency to over-race. At his best, he is certainly good enough to take this out. Selections:OUR DANCE MONKEY (1), DOLCE DRAMA (4), TALK IS CHEAP (7), REALLY SMARTIE (5)

Another strong No More Than Two Lifetime Wins event, where they compete over the mile after running very solid time over the middle distance last start. REMMINGTON (4) made a mid-race move last start and toughed it out well when fourth, and should get his chance on speed again here to be in the finish. BEARHUNTA (6) is first up in the state for visiting trainer Dean Braun and has built a handy record in his short career, despite now being a five-year-old. He strikes a tricky draw over the short distance, so it will be interesting to see how confidently they drive him from the gate, as he may be caught wide early if they push forward, but his class could still prevail. ULTIMATE GLADIATOR(8) was good first up in the state after arriving from the Riverina. He draws awkwardly on the inside of the back row, but if the gaps appear, he should again be finishing home strongly. MAXX (11) and SOHO TIGERLILY (12) have been consistent since arriving in the state but may require those up front to overdo it to bring them into the race over the short distance. TWILIGHT STORM (5) recently ran second in the Oaks and expect she may roll forward from the middle front-row draw to give herself her best chance. A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3) is another making her first start in the state and should look to find a position on speed with cover. Selections:BEARHUNTA (6), TWILIGHT STORM (5), REMMINGTON (4), ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (8)

VIVID DREAM (2) was ultra impressive first up in the state, making a dashing run from back in the field off a slippery last half and proving far too good. He takes on the older horses here but clearly looks the one to beat. I GOTTA GO (1) again draws a favourable gate after setting a hot tempo in the above race and only being beaten 10 metres. He has the gate speed to find a forward position and have options thereafter, giving him every chance to finish on the podium again. IDEN OLIVER (6) is chasing four straight victories and is putting together a very impressive record when combining with claiming driver Grace Jones. He strikes an awkward gate, but it wouldn't surprise to see them roll forward in a front row that isn't overly blessed with gate speed to give him his best chance. SHOOBEES SPIRIT (11) and MOVESLIKEALADY (12) will again be driven for their sit-sprint capabilities and should be finishing off strongly. However, there doesn't appear to be a lot of pressure up front to ensure a genuine tempo through the middle stages, which may make their task more difficult. MISS COLLANN (8) again gets her chance to improve from the nice inside back-row draw and should get every opportunity to run into a placing. Selections:VIVID DREAM (2), I GOTTA GO (1), MISS COLLANN (8), IDEN OLIVER (6)

An even field combines for the low-class race of the night, where KYRGIOS (4) produced a handy second first up for the new stable and should be further improved from that run. Expect him to settle somewhere around midfield in a front row that is blessed with plenty of gate speed from all angles when asked. PARK LANE (6) should be first to the pegs if on his best manners and could be the one at odds if he settles in running. FEELINKINDALUCKY (5) received a nice run in transit to return to the winner's circle last start. He draws awkwardly here but, with another favourable run in transit, should be right in the finish. ROSE NOIRE (7), STAROFREMEMBRANCE (8) and QUEENOFDANCE (9) are always capable of running home strongly in races of this nature. With the expected hot tempo early and KIAVINO STRIDE (10) likely to keep the speed on through the middle stages, they should get their chance to finish over the top with the right runs. Selections:KYRGIOS (4), ROSE NOIRE (7), QUEENOFDANCE (9), STAROFREMEMBRANCE (8)

A competitive 70 to 79 NR event sees EVERYTHING BUT THE (1) looking to continue his winning ways after two impressive victories of late. Expect he may again cop some early pressure from those drawn outside him, but with any luck in running, he should again be right in the finish from the nice pole draw. RAY DAN (2) resumes from a break after three handy trials and showed what he is capable of with some strong performances before heading out for a spell. He should get a nice sit on speed with cover and will be hard to hold out if fit enough. WAZZA (4) is in a similar boat being first up and draws a middle-of-the-road gate, but has a handy record overall and looks a genuine danger. GOODTIME OSCAR (3) is a tough customer and again draws nicely to find a position on speed and be battling it out over the final furlong. It wouldn't surprise to see any of the others in this field bob up if the race is run at a solid tempo, including ANOTHER NIEN (6), who is always capable of running home strongly. VANQUISH STRIDE (8), the lone runner off the back row, may be driven for a soft run along the pegs and should be finishing home strongly if the gaps appear late. Selections:EVERYTHING BUT THE (1), RAY DAN (2), GOODTIME OSCAR (3), WAZZA (4)

The open-class handicap is over the longer distance, where CUSTOM HARLEY (5) should be extremely well suited by the trip. He's a tough customer and was good when making late ground in fast time last start, and will no doubt be out there looking to out-tough his rivals again. WAVES OF CHANCE (6) returned to form when dropping back in grade over his preferred mile trip last start. He galloped away badly at his first attempt from the standing start, but may be better suited following horses out from the 10-metre handicap here. If he can settle in running, he possesses the speed to sprint home strongly late in the small field. The trio off the front row, WATERMELON SUGAR (1), IRON CLAD (2) and KEAYANG FITZY (3), continue to earn cheques for connections in this class of race without breaking through, but again get their chance with the advantage of starting off the front. POWER UP (4) is another who will need to begin better from the stand than he has in the past, but could be the one at odds finishing home strongly if he brings his best. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (7) can't be left out and, like the expected favourite CUSTOM HARLEY (5), should be very well suited by the longer distance and standing-start conditions. He should be kicking on strongly over the final stages. Selections:CUSTOM HARLEY (5), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (7), WAVES OF CHANCE (6), WATERMELON SUGAR (1)

A small field comes together for the final race of the day over the sprint trip, with numerous runners possessing good gate speed. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) looks likely to be first to the pegs and was good when third in fast time over the same journey last start. He should again run a cheeky race at odds. MISTA EAGLE (5) can also fly the gate when asked, but expect he may be driven with a sit here, knowing he is unlikely to cross his stablemate mentioned above. LAID BACK (2) showed terrific gate speed from out wide a few starts back and was only run down in good time. He draws nicely here to be right in the finish and is certainly due to break through. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1) continues to race consistently and should enjoy a solid tempo throughout, allowing him to finish home strongly if the gaps appear late. WILL HE PIKE (3) returns to the mobile after racing well from handicaps in standing-start events at his past few starts. While he also possesses very sharp gate speed when asked, expect he may be driven with a sit here in the hope of out dashing them late. MONTGOMERY BURNS (6) may need to improve on recent efforts to be in the finish but should still get his chance in the small field. CLARENDEN TRIBUTE (5) scored his first win since last year in a big way last week. He defeated SEASIDE LADY by a half neck and ran a 1.54.8 mile rate. A repeat of that run will make him hard to beat tonight. AMIRA MARIE (1) defeated FENG SHUI STAR by a neck last start after facing the breeze. She is well drawn to win again tonight. ALLORNOTHINGLEVI (2) and LINXX (10) are also chances.

CHASE THE STARS (7) returns tonight from a two year break but his form in NSW before going for a spell was good. He was a recent trial winner here at Globe Derby as well. His driver and his trainer must be respected in a race like this. DEE JAYS MISS (1) will love the inside draw and she should be able to lead. The distance is a major concern though. WATTLEBANK ARNIE (2) and HARRO HILL (8) are also chances.

STAR OF WILLOUGHBY (3) has won three of his last four starts and has really stepped his form up another level recently. He is a major chance tonight. CLARENDEN SAKURA (6), AMYS BABY ANGEL (1) and LUCKY BAMBINO (8) are also chances.

LORD ZARIAS (6) is first up from a break but he can perform better when he is fresh and early in his preparation. If he can bring his best run tonight then he is a big chance against this field. OUR INDIFFERENCE (3), ARTILLERY (5) and IM ALL BUSINESS (2) are also chances.

WELL WELL (1) will love the inside draw and the field he meets tonight. If he can hold the lead then he will be hard to run down in this sort of race. SEA HUNTER (9), PARISIAN BANDIT (7) and MEET ME AT THE BEACH (4) are also chances.

REGAL ATTIRE (10) returns from a few months off. Before going for a break he had won two of his last three starts. He is another Hryhorec runner who performs well when he is fresh. If he is anywhere near his best tonight then he should be hard to beat. REOFFENDER (2) steps in class but he is racing well and he is well drawn. He will be right in the finish. THE VICARS GIRL (7) and ALL THE TRIX (8) are also chances.

KETO (6) ran a very restless race last start. He galloped during the score up and ending up facing the breeze for the trip. His run before that though was super. He finds a very winnable race tonight so it may pay to put a line through his last start. ALOHA PRINCESS (4) is first up but she has plenty of talent and she looks like the main and only danger. REACH THE PEAK (7) and A MAJOR STARR (5) look the next best.

SAMMY BARBARO (3) has been knocking on the door for another win recently and he finds a winnable draw tonight with Michael A Smith in the sulky. He is a major chance. FEEL THE MOMENT (2), KYVALLEY JAGGER (5) and QUARTARARO (6) are also chances. Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: HOORAH PHILTRA (4) has emerged as a genuine free for all pacer since joining the Ashleigh Herbertson stable in recent months and continued his rise to prominence with a good third placing in a hot event last Saturday night. There, he worked hard on a sizzling lead time and took cover on CATCH A WAVE (11) before getting home into third, beaten just 3.4m in a slick 1:50.7 mile rate. There is plenty of speed off the front line here, but he’s quick himself and you’d expect him to work to the fence. From there, whether he leads or takes cover, he looks well placed to fight out the finish. CATCH A WAVE (11) has burned for the front his last two starts for 9.1m and 5.5m defeats in fast time. He doesn’t win out of turn these days, but it’s hard to deny his class and he’s a huge factor despite the wide back row draw. WORDS (2) showed electric gate speed when he won on Aussie debut back in early August and has run well since in lesser grade than this, while SIR JIMMY (10) dominated a FFA from the top first-up in mid-July and has run creditable races since. SELECTIONS: HOORAH PHILTRA (4), CATCH A WAVE (11), WORDS (2), SIR JIMMY (10)

OVERVIEW: Host of chances here in this up-to-70 pace, but happy to have something each-way on GUNFORHIRE (6) who regains the services of Ewa Justice for this assignment. Justice has driven the Rory Coverdale-trained pacer three times at Melton for a good win, unlucky sixth and eye-catching second behind I Am The Storm on August 22. He just peaked on his run late last Friday at Geelong when he looked a winning hope at the turn, and his efforts before that at Terang and the aforementioned race at Melton were very good. Just needs some luck from the wide front row draw, but he’s got the ability. TO THE NINES (11) has come back from a break in good form with a fast-finishing second at Mildura followed by a great closing effort in the Vicbred Super Series heats when only beaten 4.4m by I Am The Storm last week at Kilmore. BROWNIESATMIDNIGHT (12) is back in the care of Team Lee after a stint in New South Wales and I liked the way he finished off in his recent trial at Terang, while LAMBRO MACH (9), likely early leader DANCE AFFAIR (3), KIA ORA BEAUTY (4), THESTATESMAN (10) and BIZZNESS CLASS (13) are others in with a major chance. SELECTIONS: GUNFORHIRE (6), TOO THE NINES (11), BROWNIESATMIDNIGHT (12), LAMBRO MACH (9)

OVERVIEW: Sticky gate, but KYVALLEY MICHAEL (8) is in good form for Brent Lilley and looks one of the key players in this 60-69 contest. He worked to the front and won in good style two starts back, and then flashed home from the rear of the field to just miss in a race won by ALDEBARAN SUSANNE (11) here in late August. He ran past SEBASTIANS BOY (4) on that occasion, but the latter’s effort was also good and he’s working towards a victory. SCAR (7) is flying for veteran trainer-driver Robert Young and won his second race in succession when finding the front at Geelong last Friday, while TICTOK (10) bombed the start there and did a great job to only be beaten 4.1m into third. She looks ready to win. The other key chance is KYVALLEY JETSTREAM (2), who draws well and has trialed up nicely with a Kilmore win and Melton second to handy mare Aldebaran Acrux ahead of this first-up assignment. SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY MICHAEL (8), SEBASTIANS BOY (4), SCAR (7), TICTOK (10)

OVERVIEW: Cracking Group 2 Vicbred 4YO mares’ final where I reckon MISS ARI (3) shapes as a great each-way bet, with perhaps a heavier focus on the place. She is a top-end mare who ran well in a heat of this series from three back the fence when a closing third to LET HER ROLL (13) and SOHO AMERICANO (12), and importantly draws to find the fence here. I’d expect her to take cover on go-forward horse WICKED CONFESSION (7), who will likely be driven confidently by Alex Ashwood. She should be in a striking position turning for home and I think she can be fighting out the finish. WICKED CONFESSION (7) was outstanding sitting parked and running hot sectionals in a heat at Kilmore when second to THE ART OF SUCCESS (11), who is a winning machine and stretched her sequence to nine. This is a big challenge from the back row, though, as it is for LET HER ROLL (13) and SOHO AMERICANO (12), who look the other key hopes. BACK: MISS ARI (3) – 1 unit (win)/2 units (place) SELECTIONS: MISS ARI (3), WICKED CONFESSION (7), THE ART OF SUCCESS (11), LET HER ROLL (13)

OVERVIEW: Emma Stewart has a mortgage on this Vicbred final for the four-year-old colts and geldings, but finding the winner is tricky. It will likely come down to the map and who finds the front, and I fancy that might ultimately be FAIRPLAY (4) for Mark Pitt. He has won all five races this campaign, including a heat of this series last week at Kilmore when he controlled things at the head of affairs. From the top, he’d be the one to beat. Stablemate APOLLOSTORM (3) absolutely rattled home for third in that same qualifier and is a very speedy conveyance who would be a huge threat if he got to the fence, THE LAST TRIP (9) has just been outstanding since joining the Stewart stable and remains unbeaten from five goes for the yard, while STORMS COLLIDE (1) heads the other winning chances given his good gate. Hard to leave out some of the others, but SEATHESTARS (2), FOX DAN (8), NEW SHUFFLE (11) and heat winner I AM THE STORM (6) must be considered for trifectas and First 4s. SELECTIONS: FAIRPLAY (4), APOLLOSTORM (3), THE LAST TRIP (9), STORMS COLLIDE (1)

OVERVIEW: The Vicbred final for the four-year-old trotting entires and geldings looks a match race between Victorian ALRIGHTY (10) and NSW visitor I AM HELLBOUND (12). I’ll lean towards the horse with the home ground advantage and seemingly better barrier. Anndy Gath’s charge has been airborne this campaign and stretched his winning sequence to four with an easy front-running success in his heat at Melton last week. I AM HELLBOUND (12) has been a great pick-up for Scott Hewitt through 2026, and showed his class with a dominant win in the other qualifier. It would be a shock if one of the two didn’t win, with IJUSTCALLEDTOSAY (13) and KARBINE (8) perhaps the leading contenders outside those after eye-catching heat runs where they closed off nicely and into the placings. SELECTIONS: ALRIGHTY (10), I AM HELLBOUND (12), IJUSTCALLEDTOSAY (13), KARBINE (8)

OVERVIEW: Another apparent match race here in the Vicbred final for four-year-old trotting mares, with heat winners GATESYS GEM (7) and I AM WILMA (11) tough to beat. The barrier draw has really favoured GATESYS GEM (7) as she is expected to work across and find the front. She won her qualifier easily and she’s the one to beat here. Like the on-top selection, I AM WILMA (11) is a Group 1 winner and claimed the other heat in easy fashion. She’s a serious danger, but the back row makes it tough. JILLIBY DREAMLOVER (12) is a star trotter from the Lee stable who did a good job to finish second in the heat behind GATESYS GEM (7), while IRON WOMEN (3) might be able to burn the gate and find the top, and from there would be a good chance of filling a First 4 spot. That said, most of these are capable of running into the back end of the top four. BACK: GATESYS GEM (7) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: GATESYS GEM (7), I AM WILMA (11), JILLIBY DREAMLOVER (12), IRON WOMEN (3)

OVERVIEW: We got a look at five of these horses in a race at Geelong last Friday that was ultimately taken out by THUNDA STRUCK (7), who sprint-laned to victory over favourite RUBYS DREAM (5). The latter was first-up there and did control things at the front, so was perhaps a little disappointing not to win. That said, I’m in her corner again as I expect she can work over and take the lead off fast starter NAKEDTRUTH (3) and prove hard to run down back from 2100m to 1720m. THUNDA STRUCK (7) must be a chance based off his win last time, QUIRKY CHARACTER (8) was back to something like his best in that aforementioned race and only went down by 1.5m after coming from off the speed, while NAKEDTRUTH (3), who maps to find the pegs and was good running second to the handy Vici Bloom last time out, and KEAYANG LAVITA (6), who ran fourth in that clash at Geelong, are other leading hopes. BACK: RUBYS DREAM (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RUBYS DREAM (5), THUNDA STRUCK (7), QUIRKY CHARACTER (8), NAKEDTRUTH (3)

OVERVIEW: HITTHEROADJACK (3) is a one-paced type of horse who has struggled to pick-up quickly from behind the leader his past two starts. He has good gate speed, and if he’s able to wrestle the front here and control things at the top, he shapes as a good value chance. He’s a veteran of 168 starts, but is still racing well to my eye. CLYMENUS (6) finished second and best of four horses that clash again here last Friday at Geelong in a race won by Ata Rangi and is going well at the moment, MIGHTY JOLT (2) has the speed to find the fence, and while he was disappointing from a spot behind the leader last time, he draws to run a forward race, while ISOLATION (4) found the front and won an easier assignment in good style at Geelong last week following a nice trial. Not much would surprise and most are winning hopes with the right trip. BACK: HITTHEROADJACK (3) – 0.5 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: HITTHEROADJACK (3), CLYMENUS (6), MIGHTY JOLT (2), ISOLATION (4)

OVERVIEW: Multiple Group 1 winner ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (4) returns for her first run since finishing a close-up fourth in the Inter Dominion Trotting Championship Grand Final at Albion Park in July. She’s a star and should lead and win this assignment as a short-priced favourite. HOPPY (6) showed exciting progression last campaign when he won two races and placed in a further two, and looks ready to enter the free-for-all ranks, FOUROUTOFFIVE (5) won brilliantly from the chair in an easier clash than this at Melton on August 29 and is a nice type, while ALDEBARAN ACRUX (3) returns to the races following a Queensland preparation that ended after one round of Inter Dom heats, but she’s a classy mare on her night and looks the other top four contender. SELECTIONS: ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (4), HOPPY (6), FOUROUTOFFIVE (5), ALDEBARAN ACRUX (3) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R4 #3 MISS ARI – 1 unit (win)/2 units (place) R7 #7 GATESYS GEM – 4 units (win) R8 #5 RUBYS DREAM – 2 units (win) R9 #3 HITTHEROADJACK – 0.5 unit (each-way) EARLY QUADDIE 2,4,9,10,11/4,6,9,10,11,12/2,4,7,8,10/3,7,11 QUADDIE 1,3,4,9/10,12/7,11,12/3,5,6,7,8 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

THE CORDINA GROUP PACE HI MANAMEISJEFF (9) makes his first appearance since June but he goes very well fresh, winning four of six attempts, and has been readied with a trial win. Owns a great record at the mile and can add to it tonight. KINGMAN (11) had his problems last campaign but is first class when right with a Victoria Cup and NZ Cup on his resume. Hasn't raced since April and cops the outside barrier but he has trialled twice and owns a good record when fresh. HEZA PUNK ROCKER (10) has been freshened since disappointing as a hot favourite last start. Was racking up the wins prior so may be worth another chance. MAX DELIGHT (8) and RIPP (2) are both exotic players.

BESTINBEDS.COM.AU PACE RAGING WHITEBAIT (1) enjoys a class drop on his recent attempts and it is worth noting he led to win at this circuit and distance the last time he raced in this grade. Has the speed to be prominent from the ace draw so could return to the winners' list. POPS JOY (4) has been racing well against the mares including a win two back at this circuit and distance and a 1.3m second last week. They were from wider draws than this. Big chance. WEONA MISS MIKI (5) draws better than last week and did a good job to win at this circuit and distance last month so could bounce back. GO WITHOUT (7) draws a few spots wider but there was merit in last week's effort for fourth.

CAMDEN TIGERS PACE SERG BLANCO (5) has switched to the powerhouse Jason Grimson yard since his last-start fourth at Wagga five weeks ago. Has performed well at this venue before and finds a suitable assignment so could kick off for the new stable with a win. SPRINGFIELD AFFAIR (9) made it three from three for Seaton Grima when he led to score by close to 5m at this circuit and distance last week. A wider draw poses more of a challenge but winning form is hard to knock. I GOT CHILLS (10) has both a class rise and a wide barrier against him but has put together three wins and two placings from his last five starts here so deserves respect. QUIET STORM (8) enjoys a class drop on last week's attempt and was going very well with a string of top-two results prior. I BREAK THE LINE (4) owns a good third-up record so could be ready to peak after two solid efforts of a spell.

REMEMBERING UNCLE IVAN PACE OUR SUNSET DELIGHT (9) has been racing well since switching to Sydney, winning at this circuit and distance last month and finishing second in both outings since. Worked from a similar barrier and dug deep to go under narrowly last time. Big chance to go one better. MAXNJAX (8) pulled up lame when fourth as favourite in his first outing for David Aiken. Draws deeper but deserves another chance. ACTION MAJOR (7) took advantage of a low draw for a fresh win at Newcastle. Draws wider but is proven second-up so could go on with it. VINCENZO (10) is worth including after boxing on for second in this grade here two back.

CLUB MENANGLE CAROUSEL FINAL Queensland Derby winner PALLADIUM (6) was a class above at this circuit and distance last week, working to the front from a wider barrier and going on to score by more than 10m. That was his first outing for eight weeks so he should only be improved and he can take advantage of a lower draw to strike again. NYMBAL (3) was another dominant winner last week, coming from a couple of spots wider to cruise home. He is unbeaten at this distance and from a favourable draw could threaten. LEXUS LOU (1) was a beaten favourite when third last week but he has the gate speed to take advantage of the inside barrier so can give a sight. VAN BASTEN (9) added to a string of wins and placings when he scored from a similar draw last week. Deserves respect as does last-start runner-up MAURLEN BOY (2) who has put a series of top-four results together, all from wider draws.

WOODLANDS STUD 3YO PACE Boom colt LOUCASSO (7) was just too good in his comeback victory here a fortnight ago when he led from this barrier and kept going. That was his first outing for nearly nine months so should only be better for it. He is two from two when second-up and has to go on top. ALERT BAY (5) stuck on well for second to Loucasso last time, only 2.8m behind him. That added to a string of top-three results including a win from wider three back. He can be competitive again. ANDRETTI (3) was a class above when he led to score easily last week at Bathurst. This is harder but he draws to go forward again. THE QUEENS GAMBIT (6) faces her toughest yet since switching from NZ but has been impressive in winning her two Australian starts so far, one at this circuit and distance when she overcome the outside barrier.

CLUB MENANGLE TROTTERS CAROUSEL FINAL ZENITH STRIDE (8) was terrific in his comeback win last week, racing three wide without cover before scoring by 2.3m at this circuit and distance. That was his first outing for the best part of three years so the hitout should have done him the world of good. Sticking with him. LOTUS LOUISE (11) has nearly 5m to make up on Zenith Stride through their last clash but he is better than that. Had enough speed to lead from wide and win here three back so is good enough with his A-game. EZRA KAI (6) has been close-up in two outings here since switching to Luke McCarthy and could be hitting his peak now. SUNNY GEE (10) will find this easier than last week's attempt and was solid when placed behind Zenith Stride prior so is worth including.

SUCCESS STUD LADYSHIP PACE BELLA DANZA (9) showed good improvement in her second outing for the Grimson yard here a fortnight ago, sticking on for second in a Listed race behind accomplished mare Lux Aerterna. Has to overcome a wide barrier but she has the gate speed to do so and is suited coming back in grade. She could be ready to strike. SPARKLING SEA (4) makes her first appearance since July's Queensland Oaks but she was readied with a nice trial. Has won six of seven attempts at this circuit and distance and is unbeaten when fresh so expect a big return. FARFALLA STRIDE (7) made a good return when runner-up last week. Draws wider but is back against the girls and has won two of three previous second-up attempts so can progress. ALFNALMA (8) cops a wider draw but her recent consistency is hard to knock. BEST BETS:

SEABREEZE LAD (1) is a talented two year old with a lot of upside. He is first up from a spell but he is well drawn and should have matured since his runs earlier in the year. He is a massive chance tonight. CRUNCH RULES (2) looks like a big danger after breaking his maiden last start here at Port Pirie. SAL WESTER (3) and TIGER MUMFF (5) are both chances as well.

FEARFULL DRAGON (3) has won his last two starts in an impressive fashion. He should be able to lead all the way today and be hard to beat again. SPORTSFLIGHT (6) returned to the winners list last start and looks like a danger again today. He races very well here at Port Pirie. GRUMPYPANTS GRACIE (2) and ITZ BLACKJACK (4) are also chances.

ALORA (3) won by 18.3 meters last start at Gawler as she returned to racing in a big way. A repeat of that run will make her awfully hard to beat today. SO SIRIUS (5) finds an easier race compared to his first two starts in South Australia. He is first up from a spell and hasn’t been seen at the trials. It may pay to watch his market moves. REPELLING (6) and MISTER QUIRK (2) are also chances.

NORMANS GIRL (6) ran a handy race first up here at Port Pirie last start when she ran second behind SPORTSFLIGHT. She will find today easier and if she can improve off that run then she will be hard to beat. MACHFREDDY (4) looks like the main danger after a strong all the way win at Gawler last start. BROBENAH GIRL (1) and I NEED AGIRLFRIEND (3) are also chances.

ELLA KATE (9) has won two of her last four starts. The draw isn’t ideal for her today but she does race well here at Port Pirie and she finds a race she can win today. WELL WELL (1), PERFECT GAMBLE (4) and KEILAH (5) are also chances.

NITEONTHETOWN (6) has the tough draw to overcome but I love the way he has been racing recently. He ran a nice race behind PLAY IT COOL last start. He could easily feature today if he gets the right run into the race. BALLADORO (3) is drawn well and was impressive at Gawler last start. INSIDER TRADING (7) and LINCS POOR BOY (2) are also chances.
